paths.name: Short-Form Clipping
paths.tagline: Turn long videos into short clips creators happily pay for.
paths.description: Podcasters, YouTubers and streamers sit on hours of long-form content they never repurpose. You find the best moments, cut them into vertical clips for TikTok, Reels and Shorts, and sell that as a done-for-you service. No audience, no camera and no paid software required.
paths.objective: Land your first paying clipping client and earn your first $500.
paths.service: Done-for-you short-form clip packs cut from a creator’s long-form content.
skills: Spotting clip-worthy moments in long-form content
Writing hooks that stop the scroll in the first 2 seconds
Editing vertical video with captions and clean pacing
Pricing and packaging a simple service
firstTasks: Watch 20 top-performing clips in one niche and note why they work
Cut your first 3 sample clips from a public podcast episode
Build a one-page portfolio with your best samples
Find 10 creators who publish long-form content but post few clips
workflow: Find a creator who publishes long-form content but posts few or weak short clips
Cut one free sample clip from their best recent episode
Send a personalized message with the sample attached
Agree on a clip pack, price and turnaround, then collect a 50% deposit
Deliver the clips, handle one round of revisions and get approval
Send the final invoice, get paid and offer a monthly retainer

paths.name: Google Business Profiles
paths.tagline: Help local businesses show up on Google Maps and get more calls.
paths.description: Most local businesses — dentists, gyms, salons, roofers, cafés — have a half-finished Google Business Profile that costs them customers every week. You audit the profile, show the owner exactly what is broken, and get paid to fix it. It is simple, repeatable work that owners immediately understand.
paths.objective: Sign your first local business client and earn your first $500.
paths.service: Google Business Profile audits and done-for-you optimization for local businesses.
skills: Reading a Google Business Profile like a customer would
Running a structured profile audit in under 20 minutes
Explaining problems in plain language owners care about
Outreach by email, phone and walk-in
Optimizing categories, services, photos and descriptions
Reporting results with simple before-and-after numbers
firstTasks: Study 5 top-ranked local profiles and note what they have in common
Pick one city and one business type to focus on
List 10 local businesses with incomplete or outdated profiles
Run your first full audit and turn it into a one-page report
workflow: Find a local business with a weak profile: few photos, missing services, unanswered reviews
Run a 20-minute audit and turn it into a one-page report
Send the audit to the owner with 3 specific problems highlighted
Walk through the fixes on a short call and agree on a price
Get manager access, complete the optimization and document before-and-after
Send the results report, get paid and offer a monthly retainer

clipping.missionTitle: Learn how clippers get paid and pick the niche you will serve.
clipping.goal: Choose your niche and set your 30-day target.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 1 lesson
tasks.description: See how the service works end to end: who buys clips, what they pay and why they would rather outsource it.

tasks.title: Pick one niche
tasks.description: Choose a niche you already watch — business podcasts, fitness, gaming, finance. Knowing the content makes finding good moments much faster.

tasks.title: Write your 30-day income target
tasks.description: Write down a specific dollar amount and how many clip packs it takes to reach it. Keep it visible on your desk or phone.

tasks.title: Block your daily work slot
tasks.description: Pick a fixed 30–60 minute slot for the next 30 days and add it to your calendar.

clipping.missionTitle: Break down 20 top-performing clips in your niche.
clipping.goal: Know what a great clip looks like.

tasks.title: Collect 20 high-performing clips
tasks.description: Search your niche on TikTok, Reels and Shorts. Save 20 clips that clearly outperformed the account’s usual views.

tasks.title: Write down every opening line
tasks.description: Note the first sentence and first visual of each clip. This is your personal hook library.

tasks.title: Note length, captions and pacing
tasks.description: Record the duration, caption style and how often the frame changes. Look for what repeats across the winners.

tasks.title: Summarize 3 patterns
tasks.description: Write three rules you will copy in your own edits, such as “open mid-sentence on the strongest claim”.

clipping.missionTitle: Install your free tools and build a reusable clip template.
clipping.goal: Be ready to edit in under 5 minutes.

tasks.title: Install your editor
tasks.description: Set up CapCut (or the editor you prefer) on your computer or phone and sign in.

tasks.title: Create a 9:16 project template
tasks.description: Build a vertical 1080×1920 project with your caption style, font and safe margins saved as a preset.

tasks.title: Set up your folder structure
tasks.description: In Google Drive create folders: Raw, In Progress, Delivered, Portfolio. Every client will get the same structure.

tasks.title: Run a 60-second test export
tasks.description: Import any video, apply the template and export. Confirm captions are readable on your phone.

clipping.missionTitle: Edit your first complete clip from a public podcast episode.

tasks.title: Choose one long-form episode
tasks.description: Pick a recent episode in your niche that is at least 30 minutes long and mostly talking.

tasks.title: Mark 3 clip-worthy moments
tasks.description: Skim the transcript or watch at 1.5× speed. Timestamp three moments with a strong claim, story or surprising number.

tasks.title: Edit the strongest moment
tasks.description: Cut it to 30–60 seconds, reframe to vertical, remove pauses and add captions.

tasks.title: Export and watch on your phone
tasks.description: Watch it twice with sound off, then sound on. Fix anything that feels slow or hard to read.

clipping.missionTitle: Re-edit your clip with a stronger hook, then cut two more.

tasks.title: Score your clip with the hook checklist
tasks.description: Run yesterday’s clip through the checklist and note every item it fails.

tasks.title: Rewrite the first 2 seconds
tasks.description: Start on the most interesting sentence, add an on-screen headline and trim any warm-up words.

tasks.title: Cut clip number two
tasks.description: Edit the second moment you marked yesterday using your template. Aim to finish in under 20 minutes.

tasks.title: Cut clip number three
tasks.description: Edit the third moment. Try a different hook style — a question or a bold number.

clipping.missionTitle: Publish a simple one-page portfolio with your 3 best clips.
clipping.goal: Have a portfolio link you can send.

tasks.title: Follow the portfolio guide
tasks.description: Use the guide’s layout: headline, three clips, what you offer, how to contact you.

tasks.title: Upload your 3 sample clips
tasks.description: Host them in a public Drive folder or on a free page builder. Make sure they play without signing in.

tasks.title: Write a one-line offer
tasks.description: Example: “I turn your long episodes into 10 ready-to-post clips every month.” Keep it under 15 words.

tasks.title: Test the link on another device
tasks.description: Open the link on your phone in a private tab. Fix anything that is slow, broken or asks for access.

clipping.missionTitle: Find 10 creators who publish long-form content.

tasks.title: Find 10 creators
tasks.description: Search YouTube and podcast charts in your niche for creators with 5K–200K followers who post long-form weekly but few short clips.

tasks.title: Record their contact information
tasks.description: Note a business email from the channel’s About page or an open DM on their most active platform.

tasks.title: Identify their best-performing content
tasks.description: Sort their videos by most popular and note one or two episodes packed with clip-worthy moments.

tasks.title: Add them to your prospect list
tasks.description: Log each creator in your tracker with platform, audience size, contact and status “New”.

tasks.title: Send your first outreach message
tasks.description: Pick the best-fit creator and send one short, personalized message with your portfolio link. Done beats perfect.

clipping.missionTitle: Score your 10 prospects and research your top 5 in depth.
clipping.goal: Know exactly who to pitch first.

tasks.title: Score each prospect from 1 to 5
tasks.description: Rate them on posting consistency, signs of revenue (sponsors, products, courses) and how weak their current short-form is.

tasks.title: Pick your top 5
tasks.description: Move the five highest scores to the top of your tracker. These get your best effort this week.

tasks.title: Watch one recent episode each
tasks.description: Watch at 1.5× speed and timestamp two moments per creator that would make strong clips.

tasks.title: Write one personal detail per creator
tasks.description: Note a specific thing you genuinely liked — a story, a guest, a line. You will use it in your pitch.

clipping.missionTitle: Write a short, personal pitch you can adapt for every creator.
clipping.goal: Have 1 master message and 5 personalized versions.

tasks.title: Study the outreach template
tasks.description: Read the cold outreach template and highlight the four parts: personal opener, observation, offer, easy next step.

tasks.title: Write your master message
tasks.description: Draft your own version in under 90 words. No life story, no long list of services.

tasks.title: Personalize it for your top 5
tasks.description: Swap in the personal detail and the specific episode moment you found yesterday.

tasks.title: Read each message out loud
tasks.description: If a sentence sounds like an advert, rewrite it the way you would say it to a friend.

clipping.missionTitle: Send a personalized pitch to every creator on your list.

tasks.title: Send your top 5 pitches
tasks.description: Send the five messages you personalized yesterday through the contact channel you recorded.

tasks.title: Personalize and send 5 more
tasks.description: Work through the rest of your list. Spend no more than 5 minutes per message.

tasks.title: Log every message in your tracker
tasks.description: Update status to “Contacted”, add today’s date and set a follow-up date 3 days out.

tasks.title: Add 5 new creators to your list
tasks.description: Your pipeline should never be empty. Add five fresh prospects to replace the ones you just contacted.

clipping.missionTitle: Cut a free sample clip for your two best prospects and send it.

tasks.title: Pick your 2 best-fit prospects
tasks.description: Choose creators who have not replied yet but score highest in your tracker.

tasks.title: Cut one clip from each creator’s episode
tasks.description: Use the moments you already timestamped. Keep each edit under 25 minutes.

tasks.title: Check each clip against the hook checklist
tasks.description: Make sure the first 2 seconds earn the next 10 before you send anything.

tasks.title: Send the clip with a two-line message
tasks.description: Example: “Made this from your latest episode — yours to post, no strings. Happy to do 10 like this every month.”

clipping.missionTitle: Build your starter clip pack and decide your prices.

tasks.title: Run the pricing calculator
tasks.description: Enter your time per clip and income target to get a minimum price per clip.

tasks.title: Define your starter pack
tasks.description: Example: 5 clips from one episode, captions included, 1 revision round, delivered in 4 days, $150.

tasks.title: Add two higher tiers
tasks.description: Create a 10-clip pack and a monthly option so the starter pack feels like the easy first step.

tasks.title: Practice saying your price
tasks.description: Say the price out loud five times, then stop talking. No apology, no discount in the same breath.

clipping.missionTitle: Follow up with every creator who has not replied.
clipping.goal: Send a follow-up to every open prospect.

tasks.title: Filter your tracker for “Contacted”
tasks.description: List everyone you messaged 3 or more days ago who has not answered.

tasks.title: Send a value-first follow-up
tasks.description: Use the follow-up script: a new clip idea or observation, not “just checking in”.

tasks.title: Schedule follow-up number two
tasks.description: Set the next follow-up date 4 days out for everyone you contacted today.

tasks.title: Reply to anyone who answered
tasks.description: Respond within the hour if you can. Answer their question and suggest one clear next step.

clipping.missionTitle: Add 10 new creators and pitch them all today.

tasks.title: Review your week 2 numbers
tasks.description: Count messages sent, replies and positive replies. Note which opener got the most answers.

tasks.title: Find 10 new creators
tasks.description: Try a second source today: podcast guest lists, “similar channels” or newsletter sponsors in your niche.

tasks.title: Send 10 personalized pitches
tasks.description: Reuse your best-performing opener and personalize one line per creator.

tasks.title: Update your tracker
tasks.description: Log every new prospect with status, date and next follow-up.

tasks.title: Plan next week’s work slots
tasks.description: Week 3 involves calls and delivery. Block the time now so client work never slips.

clipping.missionTitle: Answer every reply and book at least one discovery call.

tasks.title: Sort replies into three groups
tasks.description: Interested, curious and not now. Update each prospect’s status in your tracker.

tasks.title: Offer two specific call times
tasks.description: To every interested creator send two 15-minute slots in their time zone. Specific times get booked; “whenever works” does not.

tasks.title: Answer curious replies with proof
tasks.description: Send your portfolio link and one sample relevant to their niche, then ask a single question about their current posting.

tasks.title: Follow up with the silent ones
tasks.description: Send your second follow-up to anyone still quiet after 7 days.

clipping.missionTitle: Prepare and run a 15-minute discovery call.
clipping.goal: Understand what the creator really wants.

tasks.title: Pick your 6 discovery questions
tasks.description: Choose questions about their goals, current workflow, posting frequency and what has not worked before.

tasks.title: Do a 10-minute practice run
tasks.description: Record yourself asking the questions and stating your price. Listen back once.

tasks.title: Run the call and mostly listen
tasks.description: Aim to talk less than 40% of the time. Write down their exact words — you will reuse them in the proposal.

tasks.title: End with a clear next step
tasks.description: Say: “I’ll send a short proposal by tomorrow noon.” If no call is booked yet, run the practice call with a friend.

clipping.missionTitle: Write and send a one-page proposal within 24 hours of the call.

tasks.title: Fill in the proposal template
tasks.description: Cover their goal in their own words, what you deliver, timeline, price and how to start.

tasks.title: Offer two options
tasks.description: Present a starter pack and a larger pack. Two options turn “yes or no” into “which one”.

tasks.title: State payment terms clearly
tasks.description: 50% deposit to start, 50% on delivery. Include exactly how they can pay.

tasks.title: Send it and set a follow-up
tasks.description: Send the proposal with a two-line message and add a follow-up reminder for 48 hours later.

clipping.missionTitle: Respond to hesitation with confidence and ask for the deal.
clipping.goal: Get a clear yes or no.

tasks.title: Prepare answers to the 4 common objections
tasks.description: “Too expensive”, “I’ll think about it”, “I have an editor”, “not right now”. Write your answer to each.

tasks.title: Follow up on your open proposal
tasks.description: Ask one direct question: “Is there anything stopping you from starting this week?”

tasks.title: Offer a low-risk first step
tasks.description: If they hesitate, propose a smaller paid trial — 3 clips from one episode — rather than dropping your price.

tasks.title: Send the deposit invoice
tasks.description: The moment they say yes, send the invoice for the 50% deposit. Momentum closes deals.

tasks.title: Pitch 5 new creators
tasks.description: Closing takes days. Keep the pipeline moving with five fresh messages.

clipping.missionTitle: Set up a smooth start: files, brand style and expectations.
clipping.goal: Have everything you need to start editing.

tasks.title: Send the onboarding checklist
tasks.description: Ask for raw files, brand fonts and colors, caption preferences and accounts they like the look of.

tasks.title: Create the shared client folder
tasks.description: Duplicate your folder structure in Drive and share it with edit access.

tasks.title: Confirm scope in writing
tasks.description: One message: number of clips, delivery date, one revision round, how feedback should be sent.

tasks.title: Build their caption preset
tasks.description: Set up a project template with their font, colors and logo so every clip is on-brand from the first draft.

clipping.missionTitle: Edit and deliver the clip pack on time.
clipping.goal: Deliver the first batch of clips.

tasks.title: Select the moments first
tasks.description: Timestamp all moments before opening the editor. Choose more than you need and keep the strongest.

tasks.title: Batch your edit
tasks.description: Do all cuts, then all reframing, then all captions. Batching is far faster than finishing one clip at a time.

tasks.title: Quality-check every clip
tasks.description: Check hook, caption spelling, audio levels and the final frame. Watch each clip once on your phone.

tasks.title: Deliver with suggested captions
tasks.description: Upload to the Delivered folder and include a suggested post caption and title for each clip.

tasks.title: No client yet? Deliver a mock pack
tasks.description: Cut a 5-clip pack for your warmest prospect and send it as a final, generous pitch.

clipping.missionTitle: Handle feedback professionally and send your final invoice.

tasks.title: Collect feedback in one place
tasks.description: Ask the client to list all changes with timestamps in a single document or message, not across five chats.

tasks.title: Complete revisions within 24 hours
tasks.description: Fast revisions are the cheapest way to look professional. Make the changes and re-deliver.

tasks.title: Get written approval
tasks.description: Ask: “Are these approved to post?” A clear yes closes the project and triggers the invoice.

tasks.title: Send the final invoice
tasks.description: Send the remaining 50% with a due date of 3 days and your payment details.

tasks.title: Log the deal in your revenue tracker
tasks.description: Record the amount as Booked, then Collected once the money arrives.

clipping.missionTitle: Ask your client for a testimonial and add it to your portfolio.

tasks.title: Send the testimonial request
tasks.description: Ask three short questions so the client only has to answer, not write from scratch.

tasks.title: Ask permission to show the clips
tasks.description: Get a clear yes to feature the delivered clips in your portfolio.

tasks.title: Update your portfolio
tasks.description: Add the testimonial and the best client clip above your sample work.

tasks.title: No client yet? Get peer feedback
tasks.description: Ask a creator who received your free sample for one sentence of feedback you can quote.

clipping.missionTitle: Send your client a short performance report on the clips.
clipping.goal: Show the value of your work in numbers.

tasks.title: Collect the numbers
tasks.description: Ask the client for views, watch time and follower change on each posted clip, or read them from the public posts.

tasks.title: Identify the top performer
tasks.description: Note what made the best clip work — topic, hook, length — in one or two sentences.

tasks.title: Write a five-line report
tasks.description: Total views, best clip, what you learned, what you would do next. Keep it readable in 30 seconds.

tasks.title: Suggest next month’s clip ideas
tasks.description: List three upcoming episodes or themes you would clip next. This sets up tomorrow’s retainer pitch.

clipping.missionTitle: Offer your client an ongoing monthly clipping package.

tasks.title: Design your retainer
tasks.description: Example: 12 clips per month, weekly delivery, priority turnaround, $450/month.

tasks.title: Write the pitch
tasks.description: Lead with the results from yesterday’s report, then present the retainer as the way to keep them coming.

tasks.title: Send it to your client
tasks.description: Send the pitch and propose a start date. Make saying yes a one-word reply.

tasks.title: Offer it to warm prospects too
tasks.description: Send a retainer-first version to two prospects who replied but never bought a pack.

clipping.missionTitle: Add two simple upsells to your offer and present one.

tasks.title: Choose 2 upsells
tasks.description: Pick from the guide: post captions and titles, scheduling, cover frames, or a second platform format.

tasks.title: Price each upsell
tasks.description: Price by the time it takes you. Most add-ons should sit between $40 and $120.

tasks.title: Add them to your proposal template
tasks.description: List them as optional add-ons under your main packages.

tasks.title: Offer one upsell to a client or prospect
tasks.description: Mention the single add-on most relevant to a problem they already told you about.

clipping.missionTitle: Turn one happy contact into introductions to new creators.

tasks.title: Write your referral ask
tasks.description: Keep it specific: “Do you know one or two creators with a podcast who would want clips like yours?”

tasks.title: Send it to your client
tasks.description: Ask right after a win — a good report or an approved delivery — when goodwill is highest.

tasks.title: Ask podcast guests and collaborators
tasks.description: Guests on your client’s show are warm leads. Message two of them mentioning the episode you clipped.

tasks.title: Log referrals in your tracker
tasks.description: Add each referred creator with the source noted so you can thank the person who introduced you.

clipping.missionTitle: Turn your delivery process into a repeatable checklist.
clipping.goal: Cut your time per clip by 25%.

tasks.title: Time one full clip edit
tasks.description: Use a stopwatch and note how long selection, cutting, captions and export each take.

tasks.title: Write your delivery checklist
tasks.description: Document every step from receiving footage to sending the invoice, in order.

tasks.title: Save presets for the slowest step
tasks.description: Create caption, zoom and export presets for whatever took longest in your timing.

tasks.title: Save your best messages as templates
tasks.description: Store your top outreach, follow-up, onboarding and delivery messages where you can paste them in seconds.

clipping.missionTitle: Run a focused outreach sprint using what has worked so far.

tasks.title: Find your best-performing message
tasks.description: Check your tracker: which opener and which type of creator produced the most replies?

tasks.title: Build a list of 15 look-alike creators
tasks.description: Find creators similar to those who replied — same niche, same size, same format.

tasks.title: Send 15 personalized pitches
tasks.description: Lead with your testimonial or best result. Keep personalization to one genuine line each.

tasks.title: Schedule every follow-up
tasks.description: Add follow-up dates for all 15 so none of today’s work is wasted.

clipping.theme: Plan Your Week Like a Business
clipping.missionTitle: Design a weekly schedule that balances delivery and sales.

tasks.title: Split your week into three blocks
tasks.description: Assign fixed days or hours to outreach, editing and admin. Outreach happens every week, even when you are busy.

tasks.title: Set weekly minimums
tasks.description: Example: 20 pitches, 10 follow-ups, all deliveries on time. Write them where you will see them.

tasks.title: Decide your capacity
tasks.description: Work out how many clips per week you can deliver well, and therefore how many clients you can take.

tasks.title: Clear your open loops
tasks.description: Reply to every unanswered message and send every overdue follow-up or invoice today.

clipping.missionTitle: Review your 30 days, celebrate your progress and set your next target.
clipping.goal: Finish the program with a clear 30-day plan.

tasks.title: Add up your numbers
tasks.description: Total prospects, messages, replies, calls, clients and revenue. Compare them with your Day 1 target.

tasks.title: Write down 3 lessons
tasks.description: What worked, what did not and what you would do differently. Be specific — name the message, the niche, the price.

tasks.title: Celebrate the win
tasks.description: You built a service, a portfolio and a pipeline from nothing in 30 days. Share the result with someone who supported you.

tasks.title: Set your next 30-day revenue goal
tasks.description: Pick a number, then work backwards to the clients, calls and pitches it requires.

tasks.title: Schedule tomorrow’s outreach block
tasks.description: Put the first work session of your next 30 days in the calendar before you close the app.

gbp.missionTitle: Study 5 live Google Business Profiles and note what the best ones do differently.
gbp.goal: Know what a strong profile looks like.

tasks.title: Watch today's lesson
tasks.description: Learn how a Google Business Profile drives calls, direction requests and bookings for a local business.

tasks.title: Search "dentist near me" on Google Maps
tasks.description: Open the top 3 results and the 3 at the bottom of the list. Look at photos, reviews, hours and services side by side.

tasks.title: Write down 5 differences
tasks.description: List five things the top-ranked profiles have that the bottom ones are missing, such as recent photos or owner replies to reviews.

tasks.title: Plan your 30 days
tasks.description: Block a fixed daily time slot for your missions so the work actually happens.

gbp.missionTitle: Pick one business type and one city to focus on for the next 30 days.
gbp.goal: Commit to one niche and one area.

tasks.title: Shortlist 3 business types
tasks.description: Choose from niches where one new customer is worth a lot: dentists, gyms, salons, roofers, cafés. Write down your top three.

tasks.title: Check the opportunity in your city
tasks.description: Search each niche on Google Maps and count how many profiles have under 50 reviews or fewer than 10 photos.

tasks.title: Pick one niche and one area
tasks.description: Choose the niche with the most weak profiles. One niche makes your audits faster and your messages sharper.

tasks.title: Write your one-line offer
tasks.description: Finish this sentence: "I help [niche] in [city] get more calls from Google by fixing their Business Profile."

gbp.missionTitle: Find 10 local businesses with weak Google Business Profiles.

tasks.title: Run 3 Google Maps searches
tasks.description: Search your niche plus your city, then two nearby neighborhoods. Scroll past the top 5 — your prospects are on page two.

tasks.title: Spot the weak signals
tasks.description: Look for a rating under 4.3, fewer than 40 reviews, no owner replies, missing hours or old photos.

tasks.title: Save 10 businesses
tasks.description: Add each business to your tracker with its name, rating, review count and Maps link.

tasks.title: Find a contact for each
tasks.description: Look for the owner or manager name on the website, Instagram or Facebook page, plus an email or phone number.

gbp.missionTitle: Grow your prospect list to 25 businesses and rank them by opportunity.

tasks.title: Add 15 more businesses
tasks.description: Repeat yesterday's searches in new neighborhoods until your tracker holds 25 businesses.

tasks.title: Check that they are real buyers
tasks.description: Remove chains and franchises. Keep owner-run businesses that are clearly open and active, like Luna Beauty Studio or Peakline Roofing.

tasks.title: Rank by opportunity
tasks.description: Tag each prospect A, B or C. A means an obvious profile problem and a contact you can actually reach.

tasks.title: Note one visible problem per A-prospect
tasks.description: Write a single specific issue next to each A-prospect, such as "no photos since 2023" or "12 unanswered reviews".

gbp.missionTitle: Complete your first full profile audit using the audit template.

tasks.title: Open the audit template
tasks.description: Read through the scoring sections: info, categories, photos, reviews, posts and services.

tasks.title: Audit a practice business
tasks.description: Pick one business from your C-list and score every section out of 10. Practice here, not on your best prospects.

tasks.title: Compare with the top competitor
tasks.description: Open the #1 ranked competitor in the same search and note review count, photo count and categories side by side.

tasks.title: Write the 3 biggest fixes
tasks.description: Summarize the three changes that would make the biggest difference, in plain words a business owner would understand.

gbp.missionTitle: Audit 3 local business profiles and score each one.

tasks.title: Set a 15-minute timer per audit
tasks.description: Speed matters. A useful audit takes 15 minutes, not two hours.

tasks.title: Audit 3 A-list prospects
tasks.description: Use the template on three of your best prospects and give each an overall score out of 100.

tasks.title: Take before screenshots
tasks.description: Screenshot each profile's main panel, photos tab and review summary. You will use these in your audit and later as before/after proof.

tasks.title: Save scores in your tracker
tasks.description: Add the audit score and top problem to each prospect so everything lives in one place.

gbp.missionTitle: Review your week, tighten your prospect list and define your starter offer.
gbp.goal: Finish week 1 with a clear offer.

tasks.title: Count your numbers
tasks.description: Write down how many prospects you found, how many audits you finished and how long each audit took.

tasks.title: Define your starter offer
tasks.description: Write what is included in your "Google Business Profile Optimization": info fixes, categories, 10 new photos, services, review replies, 4 posts.

tasks.title: Clean your list
tasks.description: Delete prospects with no reachable contact and promote the strongest B-prospects to your A-list.

tasks.title: Plan week 2
tasks.description: Block time for outreach next week. Most of your results will come from messages sent, not more research.

gbp.missionTitle: Identify the most costly problem on 5 prospect profiles and explain it in one sentence.

tasks.title: Learn the 8 common problems
tasks.description: Wrong category, missing hours, few photos, unanswered reviews, no services, no posts, low rating, inconsistent address or phone.

tasks.title: Pick the #1 problem for 5 prospects
tasks.description: Choose the single issue that most likely costs them customers, not the longest list of issues.

tasks.title: Translate into lost customers
tasks.description: Rewrite each problem as a consequence, like "Northstar Fitness shows no hours on Sunday, so people pick the gym that does."

tasks.title: Add the sentences to your tracker
tasks.description: Save each one-sentence problem next to the prospect. These become the first line of your outreach.

gbp.missionTitle: Turn your best audit into a clean one-page document you can send to a business owner.

tasks.title: Choose your strongest prospect
tasks.description: Pick the A-prospect with the clearest gap versus competitors, for example Oak & Stone Dental with 31 reviews against a rival with 240.

tasks.title: Build the one-page audit
tasks.description: Include the overall score, 3 problems with screenshots, a competitor comparison and 3 recommended fixes.

tasks.title: Cut the jargon
tasks.description: Replace terms like "NAP consistency" with plain words. The owner should understand every line in 60 seconds.

tasks.title: Export as PDF
tasks.description: Save it as a PDF named after the business. This file is your foot in the door.

tasks.title: Create 2 more audits
tasks.description: Reuse your layout for two more A-prospects. The second and third take half the time.

gbp.missionTitle: Send 5 personalized outreach messages offering a free profile audit.

tasks.title: Adapt the outreach script
tasks.description: Start with their specific problem, mention one competitor and offer to send the free audit. Keep it under 80 words.

tasks.title: Personalize 5 messages
tasks.description: Use the one-sentence problems you wrote on day 8. No message should be copy-paste identical.

tasks.title: Send them
tasks.description: Use email first, then the contact form or Instagram DM if there is no email. Send before noon on a weekday.

tasks.title: Log every message
tasks.description: Mark each prospect as Contacted with today's date and set a follow-up for 3 days from now.

gbp.missionTitle: Contact 10 more businesses using email, phone or a walk-in visit.

tasks.title: Send 6 more emails or DMs
tasks.description: Use the same structure as yesterday with a fresh specific problem for each business.

tasks.title: Make 2 phone calls
tasks.description: Call during a quiet hour, ask for the owner and say you found something on their Google listing you would like to email over.

tasks.title: Visit 2 businesses in person
tasks.description: Cafés and salons respond well to walk-ins. Bring a printed audit for a place like Urban Brew Coffee and keep it to two minutes.

tasks.title: Update your tracker
tasks.description: Log the channel you used for each contact so you can see which one gets the most replies.

gbp.missionTitle: Follow up with every prospect who has not replied and send 5 new messages.
gbp.goal: Follow up with all silent prospects.

tasks.title: List everyone who has not replied
tasks.description: Filter your tracker by Contacted status and a last-contact date of 2 or more days ago.

tasks.title: Send a value-first follow-up
tasks.description: Attach the audit PDF or one screenshot this time. Give something new instead of "just checking in".

tasks.title: Send 5 new first messages
tasks.description: Keep the pipeline filling while you follow up. Pull the next five from your A and B lists.

tasks.title: Schedule follow-up number two
tasks.description: Set a second follow-up date 4 days out for everyone you messaged today.

gbp.missionTitle: Reply to every response within the day and invite interested owners to a 15-minute call.

tasks.title: Answer every reply
tasks.description: Send the audit to anyone who asked for it and thank anyone who said no. Fast replies win local deals.

tasks.title: Offer a 15-minute call
tasks.description: Propose two specific times to walk through the audit together. Specific times get more yeses than "when are you free?".

tasks.title: Prepare your discovery questions
tasks.description: Pick 5 questions about how they get customers today, what a new customer is worth and who manages their profile.

tasks.title: Update statuses
tasks.description: Move prospects to Replied or Interested and note exactly what they said.

gbp.missionTitle: Run a 60-minute outreach sprint and reach 40 total businesses contacted.

tasks.title: Refill your list
tasks.description: Add 15 fresh businesses from a neighboring area so you never run out of people to contact.

tasks.title: Send messages for 40 minutes
tasks.description: Phone on silent, one tab open. Write one specific problem line per business and send.

tasks.title: Send all due follow-ups
tasks.description: Clear every follow-up that is due today before you finish.

tasks.title: Review your reply rate
tasks.description: Divide replies by messages sent. If it is under 10%, rewrite your first line to be more specific.

tasks.title: Complete your weekly check-in
tasks.description: Note what worked, what felt hard and which channel produced the most conversations.

gbp.missionTitle: Set your one-time optimization price and your monthly management price.

tasks.title: Run the pricing calculator
tasks.description: Enter your hours per project and income goal to see a realistic price range for your first clients.

tasks.title: Set your optimization price
tasks.description: Choose one number between $200 and $400 for the one-time optimization. Start at $250 if you are unsure.

tasks.title: Set your monthly price
tasks.description: Choose a monthly management price between $100 and $250 covering posts, review replies and a monthly report.

tasks.title: Anchor it to customer value
tasks.description: Write one sentence per niche, such as "One new dental patient is worth $800+, so the optimization pays for itself with one call."

gbp.missionTitle: Create a one-page proposal you can send within an hour of any call.

tasks.title: Fill in the proposal template
tasks.description: Add the problem, what you will fix, the timeline (7 days), the price and the next step.

tasks.title: List your deliverables
tasks.description: Copy the exact items from your optimization checklist so the client knows what they are paying for.

tasks.title: Add a simple guarantee
tasks.description: For example: "If your profile score has not improved by at least 25 points, I keep working at no extra cost."

tasks.title: Customize it for your warmest prospect
tasks.description: Fill in their business name, audit findings and competitor numbers so it is ready to send.

gbp.missionTitle: Run or rehearse a 15-minute audit walkthrough call that ends with a clear offer.

tasks.title: Learn the 4-step call structure
tasks.description: Ask questions, show the audit, present the fix, state the price. Then stop talking.

tasks.title: Rehearse out loud once
tasks.description: Record yourself walking through an audit for Peakline Roofing. Listen back and cut anything that sounds unsure.

tasks.title: Run the call or book one
tasks.description: If a prospect is interested, do the call today. If not, send 5 messages offering a specific time this week.

tasks.title: Send the proposal within an hour
tasks.description: Email the proposal right after the call while the conversation is fresh.

gbp.missionTitle: Prepare answers to the 5 most common objections and re-engage 3 stalled prospects.

tasks.title: Read the objection script
tasks.description: Cover "too expensive", "my nephew handles it", "we already rank fine", "no time" and "send me more info".

tasks.title: Write your own version of each answer
tasks.description: Put each reply in your own words so it sounds like you, not a script.

tasks.title: Message 3 stalled prospects
tasks.description: Reply to anyone who went quiet after showing interest. Reference their specific objection and offer a smaller first step.

tasks.title: Keep outreach alive
tasks.description: Send 5 new first messages. A full pipeline makes every single objection feel less heavy.

gbp.missionTitle: Set up your client onboarding process from payment to profile access.
gbp.goal: Have onboarding ready before you need it.

tasks.title: Read the onboarding checklist
tasks.description: Understand each step: agreement, invoice, access, intake questions, kickoff message.

tasks.title: Prepare your invoice
tasks.description: Create an invoice with your name, the service, the price and payment terms: 50% upfront, 50% on delivery.

tasks.title: Write the access instructions
tasks.description: Write a short step-by-step message showing the owner how to add you as a Manager on their profile. Never ask for their password.

tasks.title: Create your intake questions
tasks.description: Ask for services, service areas, opening hours, photos, and the best-selling treatment or product.

gbp.missionTitle: Build a baseline snapshot so you can prove results after the optimization.

tasks.title: List the numbers to capture
tasks.description: Rating, review count, photo count, profile views, calls, direction requests and website clicks for the last 28 days.

tasks.title: Set up the baseline page in your report
tasks.description: Add a "Before" column to your report template so every client starts with a recorded baseline.

tasks.title: Record search positions
tasks.description: Search 3 key phrases such as "roof repair [city]" in an incognito window and note where the business appears.

tasks.title: Practice on a real profile
tasks.description: Capture a full baseline for your warmest prospect so you can start the moment they say yes.

gbp.missionTitle: Make a direct offer to every interested prospect and ask for a decision.

tasks.title: List every warm prospect
tasks.description: Anyone who replied, took a call or opened your audit counts. Aim for at least 5 names.

tasks.title: Send a direct offer
tasks.description: Message each one: what you will fix, the price, the 7-day timeline, and "Shall I send the invoice so we can start Monday?"

tasks.title: Offer a first-client rate if needed
tasks.description: If you have no client yet, offer 2 spots at $200 in exchange for a testimonial. Never work for free.

tasks.title: Send the invoice on a yes
tasks.description: Send the invoice and access instructions within the hour. Momentum closes deals.

tasks.title: Complete your weekly check-in
tasks.description: Record calls held, proposals sent and money booked this week.

gbp.missionTitle: Fix the core information on a profile: categories, description, hours and services.

tasks.title: Work through the checklist
tasks.description: Open the optimization checklist and start at the top. No client yet? Do this as a written plan for your warmest prospect.

tasks.title: Fix primary and secondary categories
tasks.description: Match the primary category to the top 3 competitors and add up to 4 relevant secondary categories.

tasks.title: Rewrite the business description
tasks.description: Write 600–750 characters covering what they do, who for, the areas served and what makes them different.

tasks.title: Complete hours, services and attributes
tasks.description: Add holiday hours, every service with a short description, and attributes like wheelchair access or online booking.

gbp.missionTitle: Upload 10 quality photos and schedule 4 weekly Google posts.

tasks.title: Collect 10 strong photos
tasks.description: Ask the owner for exterior, interior, team and work photos. For Luna Beauty Studio that means the storefront, stations and finished looks.

tasks.title: Upload with a logo and cover
tasks.description: Set a clear logo and a bright cover photo first, then add the rest. Avoid stock images.

tasks.title: Write 4 Google posts
tasks.description: Write one offer, one service highlight, one team or behind-the-scenes post and one customer result. Add a call-to-action button to each.

tasks.title: Add 5 questions and answers
tasks.description: Post the questions customers really ask — parking, prices, booking — and answer them from the business account.

gbp.missionTitle: Reply to every existing review and set up a simple review request system.
gbp.goal: Start a steady flow of new reviews.

tasks.title: Reply to all unanswered reviews
tasks.description: Thank positive reviewers by name. For negative reviews, stay calm, apologize once and offer to fix it offline.

tasks.title: Create the short review link
tasks.description: Copy the profile's "Ask for reviews" link and turn it into a QR code for the front desk.

tasks.title: Give the client a request script
tasks.description: Hand over a ready-to-send text and email the staff can use right after a happy appointment.

tasks.title: Set a review target
tasks.description: Agree on a goal, such as 10 new reviews in 30 days for Oak & Stone Dental, and note it in your report.

gbp.missionTitle: Create a before-and-after report that shows the client exactly what changed.

tasks.title: Open the report template
tasks.description: Fill in the baseline numbers you captured on day 20.

tasks.title: Add before/after screenshots
tasks.description: Place the old and new profile side by side. Owners respond to pictures more than to numbers.

tasks.title: List everything you did
tasks.description: Write a plain checklist of completed work: categories fixed, 12 photos added, 18 reviews answered, 4 posts published.

tasks.title: Add 3 next-month recommendations
tasks.description: End with what should happen next, such as weekly posts, review replies and monthly photo updates. This sets up the retainer.

gbp.missionTitle: Deliver your report, send the final invoice and ask for a testimonial.

tasks.title: Walk the client through the report
tasks.description: Book 10 minutes or record a short screen video. Show the biggest win first.

tasks.title: Send the final invoice
tasks.description: Send it the same day as the report while the value is obvious.

tasks.title: Ask for a testimonial
tasks.description: Use the 3-question format so the client can answer in two minutes from their phone.

tasks.title: Ask for one referral
tasks.description: Ask: "Do you know one other business owner nearby whose Google listing could use the same help?"

gbp.missionTitle: Pitch monthly profile management to your client or warmest prospect.

tasks.title: Define your monthly package
tasks.description: Include 4 posts, all review replies within 48 hours, new photos, profile monitoring and a monthly report.

tasks.title: Adapt the retainer pitch
tasks.description: Tie the pitch to the recommendations in your report so it feels like the natural next step.

tasks.title: Send the offer
tasks.description: State the monthly price, the start date and that they can cancel any time with 30 days notice.

tasks.title: Set up a monthly routine
tasks.description: Block 2 hours per client per month in your calendar and list what happens in each block.

gbp.missionTitle: Identify one upsell for each client and restart outreach with your new proof.

tasks.title: Pick one upsell per client
tasks.description: Choose the natural add-on: review management, a second location, photo shoots or local directory listings.

tasks.title: Turn your result into a case snippet
tasks.description: Write two sentences with real numbers, like "Took a local café from 3.9 to 4.5 stars and doubled direction requests in 30 days."

tasks.title: Update your outreach script
tasks.description: Add the case snippet as the second line of your first message.

tasks.title: Send 10 new messages
tasks.description: Target the same niche as your result. Proof from a similar business is the strongest opener you have.

gbp.missionTitle: Turn your prospecting, audit and outreach work into a repeatable weekly system.

tasks.title: Write your weekly numbers
tasks.description: Set targets you control: 20 new prospects, 5 audits, 25 messages and all follow-ups cleared every week.

tasks.title: Assign tasks to days
tasks.description: For example: Monday prospecting, Tuesday audits, Wednesday and Thursday outreach, Friday follow-ups and client work.

tasks.title: Clean your tracker
tasks.description: Mark dead leads as Lost, set follow-up dates for everyone else and make sure every deal has a value.

tasks.title: Save your templates in one folder
tasks.description: Store your audit, proposal, invoice, report and scripts together so a new client takes minutes to set up.

gbp.missionTitle: Review your 30 days, celebrate your progress and set your plan for the next 30.
gbp.goal: Leave with a clear next-30-day plan.

tasks.title: Add up your numbers
tasks.description: Count prospects found, audits made, messages sent, replies, calls, clients and money earned.

tasks.title: Name your 3 biggest lessons
tasks.description: Write what worked best, what you would skip and the one skill that improved most.

tasks.title: Celebrate the progress
tasks.description: You now have a real service, real conversations and a working system. Share your win with someone who supported you.

tasks.title: Set your next-30-day target
tasks.description: Pick one revenue number and one client number, for example $1,200 and 3 retainer clients.

tasks.title: Schedule next week today
tasks.description: Block your prospecting, outreach and client hours for the next 7 days before you close the app.

resources.title: Cold Outreach Template
resources.description: A short, specific first message that works over DM or email. Swap the bracketed parts and keep it under 90 words.

sections.heading: The first message
body: Hi [first name] — I just went through [specific video / profile / page] and [one genuine, specific observation].
I noticed [the gap: e.g. "your long episodes are not being cut into shorts" / "your Google profile is missing photos and services"].
I help [type of person or business] get [result] by [your service]. I put together [a free sample / a 3-point audit] for you so you can see what I mean.
Want me to send it over? No strings attached.
— [your name]

sections.heading: Subject lines (email only)
body: Quick idea for [business or channel name]
[First name], made something for you
Noticed this on your [channel / Google profile]

sections.heading: Rules before you hit send
body: The first sentence must prove you actually looked at their work — no generic compliments.
One ask only. Do not mention price, packages, or a call in the first message.
Read it out loud. If it sounds like an ad, rewrite it like a text to a colleague.

resources.title: Client Discovery Questions
resources.description: A 15-minute call script built around questions. Ask, listen, take notes — the prospect will tell you exactly what to put in the proposal.

sections.heading: Open (2 minutes)
body: "Thanks for making time, [name]. I have about 15 minutes of questions so I can see whether I can actually help — sound good?"
"To start, tell me a bit about [the business / the channel] and where it is right now."

sections.heading: Problem and goal (8 minutes)
body: "What made you reply to my message?"
"What have you already tried for [short-form content / getting found on Google]? How did that go?"
"If this was working perfectly three months from now, what would be different?"
"What happens if it stays the way it is for the next six months?"
"Roughly what is a new [client / subscriber / customer] worth to you?"

sections.heading: Logistics (3 minutes)
body: "Besides you, is anyone else involved in deciding on something like this?"
"Do you have a budget range in mind, or would it help if I suggested a couple of options?"
"If it looks like a fit, when would you want to start?"

sections.heading: Close (2 minutes)
body: "Here is what I heard: [repeat their goal and main problem in their words]. Did I get that right?"
"I will send a short proposal by [day]. Can we agree you will give me a yes or no by [day + 3]?"

resources.title: Pricing Calculator
resources.description: Work out a floor price, a target price, and three packages from your hours and costs — so you never quote a number you will regret.

sections.heading: What to enter
body: Hours per deliverable: be honest and include revisions and client messages, not just the hands-on work.
Minimum hourly rate: the lowest figure that makes the work worth doing for you.
Monthly tool costs: editing software, caption tools, reporting tools, and so on.

sections.heading: How to read the result
body: Floor price is your walk-away number. Never go below it, even for a first client.
Target price is what you quote by default. It includes a margin for the unexpected.
The three packages are built around the target so the middle option is the natural choice.

sections.heading: Tips
body: Re-run the calculator after every project with your real hours — most beginners underestimate by 30–50%.
Raise your target price after every third client until you start hearing "no" about a third of the time.

resources.title: Proposal Template
resources.description: A one-page proposal you can send as a message, doc, or PDF. Short enough to read on a phone, clear enough to say yes to.

sections.heading: Summary
body: Proposal for [client / business name] — prepared by [your name], [date]
Where you are now: [1–2 sentences using the words they used on the call].
Where you want to be: [their goal, with a number if they gave one].
How I will help: [your service in one sentence].

sections.heading: Scope and timeline
body: What is included: [deliverable 1], [deliverable 2], [deliverable 3].
What is not included: [e.g. posting to platforms, paid ads, website changes].
Timeline: work starts on [date]; first delivery by [date]; project complete by [date].
Revisions: [number] rounds included, requested within [number] days of delivery.

sections.heading: Investment
body: Option A — [Starter name]: [scope] — $[price]
Option B — [Standard name] (recommended): [scope] — $[price]
Option C — [Premium name]: [scope] — $[price]
Payment: [50% upfront, 50% on delivery / 100% upfront for projects under $300].

sections.heading: Next step
body: To go ahead, reply with the option you want and I will send the invoice and onboarding checklist the same day.
This proposal is valid until [date].

resources.title: Follow-Up Script
resources.description: Three follow-ups on a 3-7-14 day rhythm. Each one adds something new so you never have to write "just checking in".

sections.heading: Day 3 — add value
body: Hi [first name], following up on my note from [day].
I went ahead and [made a short sample / wrote down 3 quick fixes] for [business or channel name] — [link or attached].
Happy to explain any of it if useful.

sections.heading: Day 7 — a new angle
body: Hi [first name], one more thought: [specific observation, e.g. "your competitor two streets over has 4x the photos" / "your episode with [guest] has three moments that would work as shorts"].
If it would help, I can show you what I would do in a 10-minute call this week. Does [day] or [day] work?

sections.heading: Day 14 — close the loop
body: Hi [first name], I do not want to clutter your inbox, so this is my last note for now.
If [the result] becomes a priority later, just reply to this message and I will pick it back up.
Either way, good luck with [something specific they are working on].

Invoice sent and first payment received
Start date, delivery date, and revision rounds confirmed

body: Access granted to what you need (raw footage folder / manager access to the Google Business Profile)
Brand assets received: logo, fonts, colours, example content they like
List of things to avoid: topics, words, competitors, styles

Mid-project update date added to your calendar

resources.title: Content Research Checklist
resources.description: Run through this before pitching or clipping for a creator, so you know their content well enough to pick moments that land.

sections.heading: Know the creator
body: Watched at least 2 full long-form videos or episodes
Noted their niche, audience, and the 3 topics they return to most
Checked which platforms they already post shorts on, and how often
Identified their 3 best-performing shorts and what those have in common

sections.heading: Find clip-worthy moments
body: Strong opinion or contrarian statement
A story with a clear setup and payoff under 45 seconds
A specific number, result, or before/after
A how-to step that makes sense without the rest of the video
An emotional or funny reaction

sections.heading: Log it
body: Timestamped at least 5 candidate moments per video
Rated each moment 1–3 for hook strength
Wrote a draft on-screen hook line for the top 3

resources.title: Prospect Tracker
resources.description: Your built-in pipeline: every prospect, their status, your notes, and the next follow-up date in one place.

sections.heading: How to use it daily
body: Add every prospect the moment you find them — even before you message them.
Move the status as soon as something happens: New → Contacted → Replied → Interested → Negotiating → Won or Lost.
Set a follow-up date every time you send a message. Start each day by clearing the follow-ups that are due.

sections.heading: What to write in notes
body: The specific detail you used to personalise your message.
Anything they told you about their goals, budget, or timing.
For lost deals: the reason, tagged as Timing, Budget, Fit, or Message.

sections.heading: Weekly review
body: Check your reply rate (replies ÷ contacted). Under 5% means the message needs work; over 15% means send more.
Re-open anything marked Lost for "timing" after 60 days.

resources.title: Build a Portfolio With Zero Clients
resources.description: Make 6 sample clips in a weekend that prove you can do the job — without having been hired yet.

sections.heading: Pick the right source material
body: Choose 2–3 creators in the niche you want to work in, ideally ones who publish long-form content and post few or no shorts. Their back catalogue is your practice ground.
Make 2 clips per creator. That gives you 6 samples and shows you can adapt to different voices and styles.

sections.heading: Make each sample count
body: Treat every sample as paid work: a strong hook in the first 2 seconds, accurate captions, tight cuts, vertical framing that keeps the speaker centred.
Keep clips between 20 and 45 seconds. Shorter samples get watched to the end, which is what a busy creator will do with them.
Always label samples clearly as spec work — "Sample edit, not commissioned" — and never post them publicly as if the creator hired you.

sections.heading: Present it simply
body: Put the clips in one shared folder or a single unlisted page with a one-line description under each: the source, the hook you chose, and why.
Your best sample for a given creator doubles as your pitch: "I made this from your latest episode" is the strongest first message you can send.

resources.title: The Clipping Toolkit
resources.description: The lean set of tools you need to find, cut, caption, and deliver clips — with a free option for every step.

sections.heading: Editing
body: A free desktop editor with vertical timelines and auto-captions covers 95% of clipping work. Pick one and learn its shortcuts rather than hopping between apps.
A mobile editor is handy for quick fixes and caption tweaks, but do your main edits on a larger screen.

sections.heading: Finding moments faster
body: Use auto-generated transcripts to skim a 60-minute episode in 10 minutes. Search for phrases like "the truth is", "most people", "here is what happened".
AI highlight tools can suggest moments, but treat them as a first pass — always pick the final hook yourself.

sections.heading: Delivery and organisation
body: One shared cloud folder per client with Inputs, Drafts, and Final subfolders.
File naming: [client]_[episode]_[clip number]_[v1]. It saves hours once you have more than one client.
Export at 1080×1920, 30 fps, high bitrate. Deliver a version with captions burned in unless the client asks otherwise.

resources.title: Viral Hook Checklist
resources.description: Check every clip against this list before you export. The first two seconds decide everything.

sections.heading: First 2 seconds
body: Clip starts mid-thought — no "so", "um", or intro
On-screen hook text is 8 words or fewer
The hook creates a question the viewer wants answered
There is movement or a visual change in the first second
Speaker face is clearly visible and centred

sections.heading: Body
body: A cut, zoom, or caption change at least every 3–4 seconds
Every pause longer than half a second is removed
Captions are accurate, 2–4 words at a time, inside the safe zone
Key words are emphasised with colour or size — sparingly

sections.heading: Ending
body: The payoff promised by the hook is actually delivered
Clip ends right after the payoff — no trailing sentences
Total length is 20–45 seconds unless the story needs more

resources.title: 60-Minute Editing Workflow
resources.description: A timed, repeatable process for turning one long video into three finished clips in an hour.

sections.heading: Minutes 0–15: Find the moments
body: Skim the transcript, not the video. Mark every line that is an opinion, a number, a story, or a clear how-to step.
Shortlist five moments, then pick the three with the strongest opening line. Note the in and out timestamps.

sections.heading: Minutes 15–45: Cut and caption
body: Spend about 10 minutes per clip. Rough cut first: trim to the moment, remove pauses and filler, reframe to vertical.
Then add auto-captions and fix every error — names and niche terms are usually wrong. Add the on-screen hook line last.

sections.heading: Minutes 45–60: Polish and export
body: Watch each clip once with sound off (do the captions carry it?) and once at normal speed (any awkward cuts?).
Run the Viral Hook Checklist, export, name the files properly, and upload to the client folder with a short delivery note.

resources.title: Revision Policy Template

sections.heading: The policy

resources.title: Monthly Retainer Pitch

sections.heading: Results recap (send within 48 hours of delivery)

Early results: [specific number, e.g. "the three clips reached 18,400 views in 5 days" / "profile views are up 27% and you got 9 more calls than last month"].

sections.heading: The pitch

Each month you would get: [deliverable count, e.g. "12 clips" / "4 Google posts, review replies, and a performance report"].
That is $[price] per month — [lower per-unit cost than the one-off / includes priority turnaround].
We would start with 3 months, and you can cancel any time with 14 days notice. Want me to set it up from [date]?

resources.title: Objection Handling Script
resources.description: Calm, word-for-word responses to the five objections beginners hear most. Always acknowledge first, then ask, then answer.

sections.heading: "It is too expensive"
body: "I hear you. Can I ask — too expensive compared to what, or is it more that the budget is not there right now?"
"If budget is the issue, I can do [smaller scope] for $[lower price]. Same quality, just less of it."
"For context, you said a new [customer / sponsor] is worth around $[value]. This needs to bring in [number] to pay for itself."

sections.heading: "I need to think about it"
body: "Of course. What is the main thing you want to think through? I might be able to help right now."
"Shall I check in on [specific day]? I will hold the start date until then."

sections.heading: "I can do this myself" / "My [nephew / assistant] does it"
body: "You absolutely could. The question is whether it is the best use of your time — how many hours a week has it been getting lately?"
"Happy to work alongside them. I can handle [the part they are not doing] and hand over a simple process."

sections.heading: "You do not have much experience"

resources.title: Local Prospecting Guide
resources.description: How to find local businesses with a weak Google profile and a real reason to fix it — in about 20 minutes per batch of ten.

sections.heading: Choose where to look

Search "[category] in [town]" on Google Maps. Skip the top three results — they are usually doing fine. Your prospects live at positions 4 to 15.

sections.heading: Spot a good prospect in 60 seconds
body: Look for at least two of: fewer than 40 reviews, rating below 4.4, no owner replies, fewer than 10 photos, missing hours or services, no posts.

Then check they are a real, active business: a working website or social page, recent reviews, and a phone number that matches. Avoid chains and franchises — the local manager rarely controls the profile.

sections.heading: Reach the owner

sections.heading: Close the day
body: Tick off what got done and log your numbers: prospects added, messages sent, follow-ups done.

resources.title: The Upsell Playbook
resources.description: Practical ways to grow the value of each client without feeling pushy — when to offer more, what to offer, and how to say it.

sections.heading: Timing is everything
body: Offer more only after a visible win: a clip that outperformed their average, a jump in calls, a run of new reviews. The result does the selling for you.
Never upsell while a delivery is late or a complaint is open. Fix first, then wait for the next win.

sections.heading: What to offer
body: Clipping: more clips per month, a second platform format, thumbnail and title suggestions, scheduling and posting, a monthly performance summary.
Google Business Profiles: weekly posts, review reply management, a review-generation campaign, monthly photo refreshes, profiles for additional locations.
Pick add-ons that reuse work you already do. The best upsell adds 20% more effort for 50% more revenue.

sections.heading: How to say it
body: Frame it as a recommendation, not a sale: "Based on what worked this month, the next thing I would do is [add-on]. It would be $[price] extra per month — want me to include it from [date]?"
Give one option, not a menu. If they say no, thank them and bring it up again only when new results justify it.

Cut anything that is not needed — shorter messages get more replies.
Copy the message, send it on the right platform, then log it so the prospect moves to Contacted and a follow-up date is set.

An objection means they are still talking to you. Answer in two lines, then ask a question.

1. "Too expensive": "Totally fair. Want to start with 3 clips for $90 and see how they perform?"
2. "I already have an editor": "Great. Most editors hate clipping. I can handle only the Shorts so they can focus on the long videos."
3. "Send me more info": never send a PDF. Send one sample clip and one price, then ask "Want me to start with this week's episode?"

Next step: paste the exact objection here and I will write your reply.

text.all:
Most deals happen in the follow-up, not the first message. Use this rhythm:

1. Day 3: a short bump. "Hey, did you get a chance to look at this?"
2. Day 7: add new value. A fresh sample, a screenshot, or one specific idea.
3. Day 14: the polite close. "I will assume the timing is off. Can I check back next month?"

Keep every follow-up under 40 words and never apologize for following up. After three with no answer, mark them Lost and move on.

Next step: open Prospects, filter by Contacted, and send the Day 3 bump to everyone waiting more than three days.

No replies is a data problem, not a you problem. Check three things:

1. Volume. Fewer than 20 messages sent? You do not have a result yet. Send more.
2. First line. If it starts with "I" or your service, rewrite it to mention one specific moment from their latest video.
3. Proof. Attach a 20-second sample clip cut from their own content. It doubles reply rates.

text.all:
A no stings, and it is also normal. Expect around 9 out of 10 people to pass, even when your offer is good. A no usually means "not now", not "you are bad at this".

Do three things:

1. Reply kindly: "No problem at all. Mind if I check back in a couple of months?"
2. Ask one question: "Was it price, timing, or fit?" The answer improves your next pitch.
3. Mark them Lost and set a reminder for 60 days.

Then replace them right away. Your pipeline should never depend on one person.

Next step: add two new prospects to your list before you close the app today.

When they show interest, do not keep explaining. Close with a clear, simple step.

1. Summarize in one line: what they get, by when, for how much.
2. Ask directly: "Want me to get started this week?"
3. When they say yes, send a payment link within the hour. Ask for 50% upfront, or 100% for anything under $200.
4. Confirm in writing: scope, deadline, two rounds of revisions.

You do not need a long contract for a first small project. A clear message they reply "agreed" to is enough.

Next step: send your warmest prospect the one-line summary and the question from step 2 today.

The best time to pitch a retainer is right after you deliver and they are happy.

1. Deliver on time, then share one result: "Clip 3 already has 4,200 views."
2. Make the offer simple: "Want me to do this every month? 10 clips for $250, delivered weekly."
3. Give a reason to decide now: hold the price for clients who start this month.

Price the retainer slightly below your one-off rate. Predictable income is worth the discount.

1. Send a before and after: photos, categories, and review replies.
2. Make the offer simple: "Want me to keep this up? 4 posts, all review replies and a monthly report for $150 a month."
3. Tie it to money: one extra customer a month pays for it.

Keep the retainer small and easy to say yes to. You can raise it after three months of results.

Next step: send your current client the before and after with the monthly offer today.

That feeling is normal. Everyone who sells anything felt it before their first message. It does not go away by thinking. It goes away by sending.

A few honest facts:

1. Nobody you message will remember a clumsy DM next week.
2. You are offering to solve a real problem. That is helpful, not annoying.
3. You only need to be one step ahead of your client, not an expert.

Shrink the task until it feels easy. Not "get a client". Just "send one message".

Next step: set a 10-minute timer, send one message to the least scary prospect on your list, then come back and tell me.

messages.text: Marcus Bell wants two sample clips from his own episodes before deciding. Am I working for free?

A little, and it is worth it here. He replied, he asked for something specific, and he has 31K listeners. That is a warm lead, not a time-waster.

Set a limit: two clips, 30 seconds each, from episode 58, within 48 hours. Watermark them lightly.

Next step: block 60 minutes tomorrow and cut both clips.
He said he wants a clean look with no emojis in the captions.

Good, that is a buying signal. People only give style notes when they picture using the work. Follow it exactly: simple white captions, no emojis, no flashy zooms.

When you send them, add one line: "If you like these, I can do 8 from your back catalog for $200."
Got it. Cutting them tomorrow morning.
Perfect. Send them before noon and set a follow-up for two days later. Tell me how he reacts.
Jordan just paid the $150!! What do I do now?

Congratulations, Alex. That is your first money online, and it is real.

Now protect it:

1. Confirm in writing: 5 clips, bold captions, hook in the first 2 seconds, delivery date.
2. Deliver one day early.
3. Log the payment in Revenue so your goal tracker updates.

Next step: send Jordan the confirmation message in the next 10 minutes.
He mentioned a monthly retainer if the clips perform. When do I bring it up?

Right after delivery, while he is happy. Share one early result, then offer: "Want me to do this monthly? 10 clips for $250, delivered weekly."

Jordan agreed to the 5-clip pack for $150. How do I ask for the money without making it weird?

It is only weird if you make it vague. Be plain:

"Great, excited to start. Here is the payment link for $150. As soon as it is through I will begin, and you will have all 5 clips within 5 days."

For projects under $200, ask for 100% upfront.

One out of 12 is about 8%, which is normal for cold outreach, and that one reply is a warm one. Your message is not the problem. Volume and follow-ups are.

To push it higher:

1. Follow up on day 3 with a short bump.
2. Try the business email for anyone who has not opened your DM.
3. Attach a sample clip to every first message.

Jordan Williams replied! He said: "This is actually great. How much for a handful of these every week?" What do I say?

Scammers send vague mass messages and ask for money. You will send one specific compliment and a free sample. That is the opposite.

faqs.q: How does my path get selected?
faqs.a: Your onboarding answers decide it. We look at your skills, the time and budget you have, and how comfortable you are talking to business owners. If you enjoy video and editing, we recommend Short-Form Clipping. If you prefer structured, checklist-style work with local businesses, we recommend Google Business Profiles. You always see the reasoning, and you can pick the other path if you disagree.

Yes. Go to Profile, then Paths, and choose the other path. Your progress, prospects and revenue on each path are saved separately, so you can switch back without losing anything. We suggest giving a path at least 7 days before switching, because most people get their first reply in week two.

Each day unlocks one mission with 3 to 5 small tasks and a short lesson. Week 1 sets up your offer and prospect list, week 2 is outreach, week 3 is conversations and closing, and week 4 is delivery and repeat business. Most missions take 30 to 60 minutes. Complete a mission to earn XP and keep your streak alive.

faqs.q: How does the AI Coach work?
faqs.a: The Coach answers questions about finding clients, pricing, outreach and objections, using your path and your progress as context. Ask it in plain language, the way you would ask a mentor. In this prototype, the Coach uses a library of prepared answers rather than a live AI model, so very unusual questions get a general reply.

You keep everything: your prospects, templates, lessons and revenue tracker. You also unlock a "Next 30" plan focused on turning one-off clients into monthly retainers and raising your prices. You can also restart the program on the other path.

faqs.q: How do billing and cancellation work?
faqs.a: Premium is $19.99 per month or $149.99 per year. You can cancel any time from Profile, then Subscription. After you cancel, you keep access until the end of the period you already paid for. This prototype never charges a real card.

Your streak grows by one each day you complete at least one mission task. Miss a full calendar day and it resets to zero. Your longest streak is always kept on your Streak page, so a reset never erases your record.

No. This prototype uses fictitious data stored only on your device. The prospects, clients, messages and payments you see are made-up examples, and anything you add stays in your browser. Nothing is sent to a server.

faqs.q: Do I need to spend money on tools?
faqs.a: No. Both paths are designed to start at $0. Clipping works with free editors such as CapCut, and Google Business Profile audits only need a browser and our checklist. Paid tools are optional, and we only suggest them after your first client has paid.

faqs.q: Does FirstRevenue guarantee I will make money?
faqs.a: No, and you should be careful with anyone who does. We give you a proven daily process, scripts and coaching. Your results depend on how many people you contact and how consistently you follow up. Most beginners need 30 to 50 outreach messages to land a first client.
